Abandoned

we did not make any progress here, abandon
This seems to conflict with https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/82560 which was already moving some of the names to direct properties.  Is that a better approach?

The linked patch does not get rid of `patternProperties`. I do not want to block 82560 because of my work here so i guess it can go first since it's been up for some time.

And 82560's related patch
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/82559
has been pending for more than a month already without a single comment from dbus-sensors maintainers.

I am not sure if the 'temp' sensors are structured enough to allow dropping the names array thing. Since apparently there are now also pressure and humidity sensors managed by that reactor.

For the case of a chip exposing multiple temperature sensors we may still need some kind of array to find a `Name` for all of them.

So i guess my patch here can be considered separately from 82560.

Resolving this comment since the linked patch does not fix my issue.
Should we rebase on it?

> Should we rebase on it?

My patch does not depend on it. What do we gain by rebasing.

It's not like review will magically speed up overnight and merge both patches in a short time (in which case rebasing would make sense to avoid extra revisions due to conflicts)

Consider we have not a single comment or indication from dbus-sensors maintainers
if Naresh's patch is good to go. If i rebased my patch and they found problems with 82559 then my patch gets delayed or not reviewed at all.
Done

Not interested in breaking changes to the json format here.  These files are used in a lot of places, and causing this level of thrash by breaking all in-process files and everyones forks doesn't seem worth it for this minor of a change.

> by breaking all in-process files

Do you mean pending gerrit changes? If so, that's a normal part of development,
changes can be conflicting and one might need to rebase their patches if something else gets merged.

If that's what you mean i am not sure it counts as valid argument because you can say that about most gerrit changes. They usually have a (merge) conflict with another change.

> Not interested in breaking changes 

Can you further explain what is breaking about this change.

The dbus-sensors will still be able to consume the old-style config for TempSensor.

Or do you mean that the config validation will fail for downstream configs?

Cherry-picking an example from elsewhere in the open source ecosystem: While Linux's syscall interface has a no-regressions policy, the internal APIs are never considered stable. There are two motivations for that:

1. Ensuring that upstream developers can refactor the implementation as needs shift over time
2. To encourage contributions upstream by adding friction to keeping patches out-of-tree

I see parallels here. OpenBMC's equivalent of Linux's syscall interface is Redfish and IPMI. Anything else should be fair game, with the same motivations as Linux.

Regardless, in this case, we can provide a transitional period by implementing both approaches in the schema, the dropping `patternProperties` some time in the future. I use the overlap strategy extensively in libpldm to allow non-breaking progress.

Thanks for taking the time to review 👍

> the internal APIs are never considered stable.

IMO this is also the documented design intent of entity-manager (see `CONFIG_FORMAT.md`, committed in 21608383661285e63e97c0457f55817f6e1d6b92)

```
+3. Configuration files are not a long-term stable ABI.  Why?
+    - Configuration files occasionally need to modify their schema in pursuit of
+      simplicity, or based on a greater understanding of the system level
+      constraints.
+    - The repo will ensure that all schema changes are enacted such that the
+      files in the repo will not be broken as a result of the schema change, and
+      will be carried forward.  The recommended way to avoid merge problems is
+      to upstream your configurations.
+    - Note: This drives the requirement that config files shall not be checked
+      into OpenBMC meta layers.
```

> Regardless, in this case, we can provide a transitional period by implementing both approaches in the schema, the dropping patternProperties some time in the future. I use the overlap strategy extensively in libpldm to allow non-breaking progress.

I am wondering how this improves things for downstream users. No one needs 'time to migrate' here, it is a trivial change which is easily automated.

Anyone who wants their configurations taken care of without having to lift a finger can simply upstream them.

My intent was to make this the least breaking change possible which is why in my corresponding dbus-sensors change (see topic) the reactor still accepts the old-style configuration.

>  I use the overlap strategy extensively in libpldm to allow non-breaking progress.

IMO the progress here is removing a bad example of how not to write a config schema. The new way of using `ExtraNames` is not much better for performance, and it also does not enable any new use-cases or fix any user-visible bugs.

It is simply an effort to change EM to eventually be compatible with D-Bus and it's design intent.

IMO this falls under the documented design intent of
```
+    - Configuration files occasionally need to modify their schema in pursuit of
+      simplicity, or based on a greater understanding of the system level
+      constraints.
```
since our system-level constraint is that we are using D-Bus, so we need to adapt to D-Bus design intent and available tooling.

> We can never do refactoring 

This is taking what I said to an extreme.  What I said is that THIS specific change doesn't seem worth it.  In addition, justifying a tree-wide change because PDI can't represent a property seems suspect to me given these aren't governed by PDI.  I'm not sure how that got turned into "we can never do refactoring" but obviously that was not my intent.
Can we make the Name or Names a OneOf in the schema?  I don't really like that you have a name plus an optional array of extra ones.  I think we should either use an array or a singleton.
ping for reply on this discussion
I agree having just Name and Names together is a bit confusing, so ExtraNames makes sense to me.
Changed it to `ExtraNames`
Overall, I find the previous format easier to understand than the new format being proposed.

The previous format is not acceptable since it breaks D-Bus design intent. So we have to find a new solution.

What about something like 
```
{
  "Name": "U52",
  "ChannelNames": [
    "MB Air Inlet",
    "MB Air Outlet",
  ],
  ...
  "Type": "..."
}
```

where we do not use the `Name` property at all on the `dbus-sensors` side and instead let `Name` represent the name of the chip e.g. in the schematic.

That way the first channel does not get any 'special' treatment which is more consistent overall.

> since it breaks D-Bus design intent

These are json files, not Dbus.  Sure, we can agree that when these are converted to dbus interfaces, the properties they create are less than ideal.  That doesn't mean we need to change the json, it means we need to figure out the DBus property conversion.

> The previous format is not acceptable 

"not acceptable" is subjective,   Sure, the dbus interfaces they create are less than ideal, but they do WORK today on real systems, which is the important part.  I understand you and Patrick want to push PDI to where it wasn't before, and that's a noble goal, but these json files aren't governed by PDI, nor are the consuming daemons, so I'm not really sure the justification of that.  Lets get the commit message updated if that's your intent here.

As an abstraction, this doesn't meet the intent that they be relatively self describing.

"Name1" means "The name of the 1st input on a TMP421".

How do I know that ExtraNames, index 1 means the same thing?  A TMP421 only has 2 inputs, so making this an array means that there's another place we can now mess up the config in ways that aren't statically detectable.

If we follow the convention of PSUSensor, where we add in the types, this would become

Temp1,
Temp0,

Ect.

> How do I know that ExtraNames, index 1 means the same thing?

Added `description` property to properly document it. Sorry for just adding config properties without any documentation.

> mess up the config in ways that aren't statically detectable.

If that would have been the intent to limit the number of channel names to match the sensor type, the previous solution does not do that either.

> If we follow the convention of PSUSensor,

That's literally the worst schema that we have. I don't think there's much we can learn from it.

If we are looking for examples, then maybe device tree schemas could be worth looking at. But that's historically not really been done for EM schemas so i am not considering it here.

This is now unbounded, which gives us less safety than we had before.  If I create an array of 100000 of these, that will be parsed as valid.

Admittedly, the old format should've explicitly limited the regex more, but as written you can only go to Name99 before you get cut off.  For TMP421s, this should've realistically only allowed Name1.
It can be bounded both ways with `minItems` and `maxItems`. One or both should be required in the configuration.
Yes, nice find. Added the `maxItems` for now. In the future it could be broken down further for each temp sensor type to better validate the configuration.

For the record, the devicetree binding schema is a useful reference for this kind of thing:

https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/tree/Documentation/devicetree/bindings/example-schema.yaml?h=v6.19

There's also an instructive "dos and don'ts":

https://docs.kernel.org/devicetree/bindings/writing-bindings.html

Some of it may not be directly applicable, but both devicetree and EM configs are trying to solve related problems, and so we should adopt useful principles and techniques where possible

Because these are shared schema, you can't really define a single maxItems that applies to all chips.  TMP421 maxItems would be 1.  Other chips would be > 1.

Overall, this still results in possibly unbounded property lists, and doesn't give a definition of what each index represents.

> Because these are shared schema, you can't really define a single maxItems that applies to all chips.

This was not done previously either with the patternProperties. So there is no regression on that part.

> Overall, this still results in possibly unbounded property lists, and doesn't give a definition of what each index represents.

I did put `description` on both properties which documents that the name of first channel and additional channels are configured.

So it maps directly to linux hwmon channels like before, but now it's documented.
I'm not sure I really even understand this.  Can you put an example of what the existing dbus interface produces, and why PDI can't consume "Name1" as a property?

> I'm not sure I really even understand this.  

You do understand, we had this same discussion like 100 times already.

> and why PDI can't consume "Name1" as a property?

D-Bus interfaces have a fixed number of properties.

Another solution would be to simply put an interface with
fixed properties `Name1`, `Name2`, `Name3`, ... , `Name17`

and consume that on dbus-sensors side.
The unused names would then be empty strings and can be ignored by the client.

That way we stay D-Bus compatible and the PDI abstraction works.

But that would require build a representation of what a config record is supposed to look like on D-Bus, which is an idea you rejected previously.
